key_insight: Rule-generated fictional environments can train LLM search agents that generalize to real-world multi-hop tasks, despite containing no real facts.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a low-cost, scalable RL data source for building transferable agents without human-curated environments or LLM-generated worlds.
method: Build multi-turn RL environments from fictional worlds with templated articles.
Require agents to search the corpus and answer multi-hop questions with verifiable rewards.
Train on synthetic environments and evaluate transfer to real-world multi-hop search benchmarks.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that agents trained in PhantomEnvironments transfer well to real-world benchmarks, often beating agents trained on real-world data on newer tasks, and Qwen models scale search budget roughly linearly with question difficulty.
watch_item: Even though the environments are cheap and synthetic, transfer may depend strongly on hop count and other task design choices, so broader generalization should be validated carefully.
paper_title: PhantomEnvironments: Training LLM Agents in Fictional Worlds
